ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Synthesis and Inquiry\
As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=\frac{3}{4}x^{2}-\frac{15}{4}x+3$ intersects the x-axis at points $A$ and $B$, with point $A$ located to the left of point $B$, and intersects the y-axis at point $C$. Point $P$ starts from point $B$ and moves towards the endpoint $C$ along $BC$ at a speed of $1$ unit length per second. Simultaneously, point $Q$ starts from point $O$ and moves towards the endpoint $B$ at the same speed along the positive half of the x-axis. Once arrived, both points stop moving. Connect $PQ$. When $\triangle BPQ$ is an isosceles triangle, please directly write down the time of movement.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the motion time be $t$. According to the problem statement, in order to form $\triangle BPQ$, points P and Q must not coincide with B, hence the range of $t$ is $0<t<4$,\\
$\therefore PB=OQ=t$, $BQ=4-t$,\\
As shown in the figure, draw $PD\perp x$ axis at point D, let the coordinates of P be $\left(a, -\frac{3}{4}a+3\right)$, then $BD=4-a$, $PD=-\frac{3}{4}a+3$,\\
According to the Pythagorean theorem, in $\triangle PDB$,\\
$PD^2+DB^2=PB^2$,\\
$\left(-\frac{3}{4}a+3\right)^2+\left(4-a\right)^2=t^2$,\\
We find $a_1=4-\frac{4}{5}t$, $a_2=4+\frac{4}{5}t$ (this does not meet the conditions and is excluded),\\
$\therefore$The coordinates of point P are $\left(4-\frac{4t}{5}, \frac{3t}{5}\right)$,\\
$\because$The coordinates of point Q are $\left(t, 0\right)$,\\
$\therefore PQ^2=\left(4-\frac{4t}{5}-t\right)^2+\left(\frac{3t}{5}\right)^2=\frac{90}{25}t^2-\frac{72t}{5}+16$,\\
(1) When $BP=BQ$,\\
that is, $t=4-t$,\\
We solve: $t=\boxed{2}$;\\
(2) When $BP=PQ$,\\
$t^2=\frac{90}{25}t^2-\frac{72t}{5}+16$,\\
We solve: $t_1=\boxed{\frac{20}{13}}$, $t_2=4$ (this does not meet the conditions and is excluded),\\
(3) When $BQ=PQ$,\\
$\left(4-t\right)^2=\frac{90}{25}t^2-\frac{72t}{5}+16$,\\
We solve: $t_1=\boxed{\frac{32}{13}}$, $t_2=0$ (this does not meet the conditions and is excluded),\\
In summary: when $\triangle BPQ$ is an isosceles triangle, the times are \boxed{2} seconds, \boxed{\frac{20}{13}} seconds, \boxed{\frac{32}{13}} seconds.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the main diagram, the coordinate axes have been drawn, the parabola opens upward, and intersects the x-axis at two points A and B, with A on the left side of B; it intersects the y-axis at point C. Point P moves on the line segment from B to C, and point Q moves on the positive half-axis of the x-axis from O toward B. On the right side is a spare diagram, showing the positional relationship of the same parabola with the coordinate axes and A, B, C.
Then reason: From the parabola y=3/4x^2-15/4x+3, let y=0 to get 3x^2-15x+12=0, namely (x-1)(x-4)=0, so A=(1,0), B=(4,0); let x=0 to get C=(0,3). Therefore BC=5. Let the movement time be t, then Q starts from O with speed 1, so Q=(t,0), and to form a non-degenerate triangle, 0<t<4 is needed. P moves from B along BC at 1 unit/second, hence BP=t, and P divides BC in the ratio t/5: P=(4-4t/5, 3t/5). Thus BQ=4-t, and PQ^2=(4-4t/5-t)^2+(3t/5)^2.
Classify and discuss the isosceles triangle BPQ:
1) BP=BQ: t=4-t, obtaining t=2.
2) BP=PQ: t^2=(4-4t/5-t)^2+(3t/5)^2, simplifying gives 13t^2-72t+80=0, solving gives t=4 or t=20/13, discard t=4, obtain t=20/13.
3) BQ=PQ: (4-t)^2=(4-4t/5-t)^2+(3t/5)^2, simplifying gives 13t^2-32t=0, solving gives t=0 or t=32/13, discard t=0, obtain t=32/13.
Therefore the movement times satisfying the conditions are 2 seconds, 20/13 seconds, and 32/13 seconds.
